summary: The replacement closes the prior annotated equal-width NAME counterexample, strengthens the committed work bounds, preserves duplicate fixture invocations in C5, and shows constant real RHS split counts of 90 at n=80, n=160, and n=300. It is nevertheless blocking because the monotonic-width guard still accepts shapes whose batch partitions differ from the unchanged legacy RHS path. A default-Mode chain of 30 nondecreasing-width CJK STRING bodies enters the batch helper twice and formats to 527 bytes instead of the legacy path's 509 bytes. A broader read-only differential found 89 mismatches among 669 batch-accepted cases. The committed differential tests do not cover increasing-width STRING sequences, so exact-byte compatibility remains falsified.

falsification_attempts.probe: Differentially format candidate versus forced legacy for monotonic equal, gradually increasing, and large-jump NAME/NUMBER/STRING bodies across top-level, annotated, chained, indented, subscript-LHS, tuple-LHS, and long-LHS assignments at 18 boundary-focused line lengths. Track whether the batch helper actually accepts each case.
falsification_attempts.evidence: diff.patch and replayable QA probe P2: 669 of 1,008 cases entered the batch helper, with 89 candidate/legacy byte mismatches. At default black.Mode(), source SHA-256 abdbc21a121050dae7d8c1e55418293dcfb2beb5480d3289f4b1c3f7ee91c060 (`result = base` plus five repetitions at each successive body width of one through six CJK characters) entered the batch helper twice. Candidate output SHA-256 464f8d5fe3800b6c1baf34a5ed5c0a5266c1155070449da4ece5961e1c314acd was 527 bytes; forced legacy SHA-256 2cbedf18f345f6f7808421990222741cbc8a3c77016ed92a40cf73260bba1a9b was 509 bytes. findings.claim: The replacement's monotonic-width guard still admits simple STRING chains whose optimized partitions change exact formatting bytes relative to legacy RHS splitting.
findings.evidence: diff.patch accepts STRING bodies and permits nondecreasing trailer widths. Replayable QA probe P2 used a default-Mode top-level assignment with 30 STRING bodies: five each containing one through six CJK characters, so trailer display widths are monotonic. The helper was accepted twice. Candidate output was 527 bytes with SHA-256 464f8d5fe3800b6c1baf34a5ed5c0a5266c1155070449da4ece5961e1c314acd; forcing CannotSplit into the unchanged legacy loop produced 509 bytes with SHA-256 2cbedf18f345f6f7808421990222741cbc8a3c77016ed92a40cf73260bba1a9b. The candidate introduced four additional body splits. The broader boundary/context matrix found 89 mismatches among 669 accepted cases.

findings.claim: The committed legacy differential does not exercise nondecreasing unequal-width STRING trailers, allowing the remaining accepted-shape byte drift to pass.
findings.evidence: diff.patch parameterizes two equal-width NAME cases and one nonmonotonic NUMBER case that is rejected to fallback. It has no STRING case and no accepted gradually increasing-width sequence. C6 reports zero mismatches for its 162 cases, but replayable QA probe P2 independently finds default-mode increasing-width STRING drift and 89 total mismatches outside that matrix.
